newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run sellers look for higher prices.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run sellers look for higher prices.

text.p: European straight-run fuel sellers looked for higher prices on Tuesday as strong crude and thinner supply firmed the market, traders said.
Offer levels for low sulphur material were heard around the $112-$114 a tonne fob mark. The only buyer evident today was believed indicating $108.
Prompt availability was tight though U.S. buyers were said not to be interested at current levels, leaving the field to the Europeans.
In the Mediterranean summer flows of Russian fuel oil have begun and have met little buying interest.
"We've really got to see prices coming off before people start buying this stuff," said one trader. "You couldn't shift a cargo today, not to an end-user."
Notional price levels for M-100s in the Med were high cif quotes plus $2 and for M-40s three means plus $1 or flat.
In the north opinions differed as to how much material was reaching St.Petersburg with some seeing it steady and others still sporadic and ice or river maintenance affected.
"There is a reasonable supply of straight-run. What's lying on the market at the moment is cracked Russian material," said one trader.
